questions.question: Sam wants to measure his bed with shoeboxes. What should he do?
options: Line the boxes up end to end
Put a gap between each box
Stack the boxes on top of each other
questions.explain: To measure, you line up the same-size units end to end and count them. Gaps, overlaps, or mixing sizes make the count wrong.

questions.question: You measure a shelf with 12 blocks, one after the other. Your friend overlaps her blocks and gets 10. Who got the right length?
options: You, because you put blocks end to end
Both, because you used the same blocks
Your friend, because she was faster
questions.explain: You measured right because you put the blocks end to end. Overlapping the blocks makes the count too small, so 10 is wrong.

questions.question: To measure a string with paper clips, what is the right way?
options: Stack the clips on top of each other
Use 4 big clips and 2 small ones
Put the clips end to end and count
Leave a gap between each clip
questions.explain: You line up same-size clips end to end and count them to get the length. Gaps, overlaps, or mixing sizes change the count.

questions.question: You measure a fence with blocks, end to end. The fence is 13 blocks long. You measure a shorter fence with the same blocks and it is 8 blocks long. How many more blocks is the first fence?
questions.explain: The first fence is 13 blocks and the second is 8, so the difference is 13 minus 8, which is 5. Adding them up would give the wrong answer.

questions.question: You have 13 paper clips. You use some to measure a string, end to end. You have 4 clips left. How many clips did you use for the string?
questions.explain: You started with 13 and have 4 left, so you used 13 minus 4, which is 9. Leaving gaps would make you use more clips than you need.

questions.question: Mia measures a rope. She uses 6 big blocks and 3 small blocks and says the rope is 9 blocks long. What went wrong?
options: She left a gap between each block
She mixed big and small blocks
She put the blocks in a circle
questions.explain: All your units must be the same size to measure correctly. Big blocks and small blocks are not the same unit, so you cannot add them together.

questions.question: You measure a book with 8 crayons, end to end. You measure a longer book and it takes 3 more crayons. How long is the second book?
questions.explain: The first book is 8 crayons and the second is 3 more, so the second book is 8 plus 3, which is 11 crayons. Leaving a gap would make you count extra crayons.

questions.question: A line is made of 5 blocks placed end to end. How many blocks long is the line?
questions.explain: Count the blocks you placed end to end. There are 5, so the line is 5 blocks long. Leaving gaps between blocks makes you count fewer than you really have.

questions.question: A string is as long as 7 paper clips put end to end. How many paper clips long is the string?
questions.explain: Count each paper clip one by one. There are 7, so the string is 7 paper clips long. A gap between clips makes the count too small.

questions.question: You put 4 cubes in a row, touching, end to end. How many cubes is the row?
questions.explain: Count the cubes touching end to end. There are 4, so the row is 4 cubes long. Gaps between cubes give you the wrong count.

questions.question: A stick matches 8 toothpicks lined up end to end. How many toothpicks long is the stick?
questions.explain: Count each toothpick in the line. There are 8, so the stick is 8 toothpicks long. A gap between toothpicks makes you count fewer.

questions.question: You measure a crayon with 6 blocks, all the same size, end to end. How many blocks long is the crayon?
questions.explain: Count the blocks you placed end to end along the crayon. There are 6, so the crayon is 6 blocks long. Gaps between blocks change the count.

questions.question: Lina puts 9 buttons end to end along her shoe. How many buttons is her shoe?
questions.explain: Count the buttons Lina placed end to end. There are 9, so her shoe is 9 buttons long. Leaving gaps between buttons makes the count too small.

questions.question: You want to measure a book with blocks. Which is the right way?
questions.explain: To measure a length you put units of the same size end to end along the object. Mixing sizes or leaving gaps both give a wrong count.

questions.question: Sam measures a rope with 7 sticks, all the same size, end to end. How many sticks long is the rope?
questions.explain: Count the sticks Sam placed end to end. There are 7, so the rope is 7 sticks long. Gaps between sticks make the count too low.

questions.question: The bottom shelf is 5 blocks long and the top is 6 blocks long, both end to end. How many blocks for both shelves?
questions.explain: Add the two counts: 5 blocks for the bottom plus 6 blocks for the top makes 11 blocks. Leaving gaps would make you count fewer than you used.

questions.question: You need 12 blocks, end to end, to measure a long rope. You have 8 so far. How many more do you need?
questions.explain: You need 12 total and already have 8, so count up from 8: 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 4 more blocks.

questions.question: You measure a crayon with 4 blocks, end to end. Then you measure a ruler with 3 blocks, same size, end to end. How many blocks did you use for both?
questions.explain: Add the two counts: 4 blocks for the crayon plus 3 blocks for the ruler makes 7. Counting one too few, like leaving a gap, gives the wrong total.

questions.question: You measure a pencil with 3 paper clips and 2 big blocks, end to end. Your friend says it is 5 units long. What went wrong?
questions.explain: Paper clips and blocks are different sizes, so they are not the same unit. To measure a length, all units must be the same size placed end to end.
